subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — next steps
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Park <emily.park@nimbushealth.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: POC success criteria & KPIs — proposed next steps

Hi Emily —

Great to meet you and Raj on today's discovery call. Quick recap and proposed next steps to get the POC scoped and scheduled: 

Recap (high level):
- Primary use case: patient intake triage + routing (short-form clinical notes -> structured attributes + intent).
- Key constraints: 95th latency sensitivity for real-time UX, mixed short/medium token lengths (avg 120 tokens per request), security/compliance required (HIPAA discussions ongoing).

Proposed POC success criteria / KPIs (please review & adjust):
1) Latency: p95 generation latency <= 200ms for 4k-context model with typical 120-token requests.
2) Throughput: sustain 100 requests/sec (concurrent window) with 99% availability during test windows.
3) Cost: average cost per 1k tokens <= $0.80 (i.e., $0.0008 / token) for production-feasible mode.
4) Quality: intent classification accuracy >= 92% on your labeled eval set; entity extraction F1 >= 0.90; hallucination rate < 1% on spot-checks.
5) Reliability: zero-severity incidents that cause downtime during core business hours for the duration of the trial.

Evaluation plan / measurement:
- Redwood will provide an evaluation harness and logging that emits per-request latency, token counts, and cost estimates.
- We suggest a shared eval set of ~1,000 representative examples you provide. We'll run the model against baseline and proposed config and produce a KPI report.

Proposed timeline & ownership:
- Share eval set (Customer) — due: 2027-03-04 — owner: Emily (Nimbus Health)
- Redwood to provision POC environment & baseline config — by: 2027-03-08 — owner: Jordan (Redwood)
- 2-week active trial window: 2027-03-08 -> 2027-03-22 — weekly check-ins (Fridays) — owner: Jordan / Lauren
- Final KPI report and decision meeting — by: 2027-03-25 — owners: Jordan + Emily

Attachments: POC plan draft attached.

Next steps: Can you confirm the eval set timeline and whether the throughput target should be adjusted to 50 req/s vs 100 req/s given expected concurrency? Also let me know any additional security evidence you need up front.

Thanks,
Jordan Blake
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
[jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com]
[Attachment: redwood_poc_plan.pdf]

From: Emily Park <emily.park@nimbushealth.com>

Date: Mon, 01 Mar 2027 13:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — proposed next steps

Thanks Jordan — appreciate the clear summary. A few quick notes: 

- The proposed KPIs look reasonable overall. Our immediate ask is more weighted toward accuracy / quality rather than raw throughput. We expect peak concurrency ~60 concurrent users; sustained traffic probably around 40 req/s. Can we set throughput target to 50 req/s for the POC and then measure scale?
- For latency, 200ms p95 is ambitious for our current UX; can you confirm whether that number assumes batching / KV cache and whether it applies to generation only (not including network overhead)?
- For quality measurement: we can share an initial eval set of ~800 labeled examples this week. Attached are some sample transcripts and labels so you can validate the schemas we use.

We can confirm the eval set by EOD on 2027-03-04 and aim to start the environment on 2027-03-08. Weekly Friday syncs work for us.

Also, we will need a short note on how you measure hallucination rate and what you consider a false positive for intent classification.

Best,
Emily Park
Head of Clinical AI | Nimbus Health
[emily.park@nimbushealth.com]
[Attachment: nimbus_sample_transcripts.csv]

Subject: Re: POC success criteria & KPIs — proposed next steps

Hi Emily —

Thanks for the quick reply and the sample transcripts — those look great and will help shape the eval harness. A few clarifications below: 

Latency: Our 200ms p95 estimate is for model-generation time on a typical GPU-backed runtime (measured server-side, excluding client network latency). That target assumes lightweight prompts (your average 120 tokens) and uses prefix KV caching where applicable. If you expect many longer sequences (>500 tokens) we should re-baseline.

Throughput: Setting the POC target to 50 req/s is fine. We will provision capacity for a 2x buffer (100 req/s) but validate at 50 req/s sustained for a fair test.

Quality / hallucination metric: We use a combination of automated checks (entity overlap, confidence thresholds) and manual spot-checks. Hallucination rate for the POC will be operationally defined as the percentage of generated responses with fabricated entities relative to the ground-truth label set on a 500-sample spot-check. We'll provide the rubric in the shared doc.

Eval harness & reporting: We'll create a shared Google Doc with the rubric and a lightweight script that takes your labeled CSV and outputs per-example metrics (intent accuracy, entity F1, hallucination flags) + aggregate KPI table. Link below once ready.

Next steps (updated):
- Emily: confirm eval set by 2027-03-04 (owner: Emily)
- Jordan: share evaluation harness + rubric by 2027-03-05 (owner: Jordan)
- Redwood: provision POC environment by 2027-03-08 (owner: Jordan / Lauren)
- Weekly Friday syncs during trial (owner: Jordan)

I'll drop the eval harness link in the doc by EOD tomorrow.

Thanks,
Jordan

Hi team — looping in operational details from Redwood Dedicated side so the POC is smooth. A couple asks for sizing & provisioning: 

1) Expected concurrency and average tokens per request (Emily, you mentioned ~60 concurrent users and ~120 tokens average) — please confirm.
2) Expected daily test traffic profile (spiky vs steady) — helps us decide autoscaling and batch windows.
3) Will you need a dedicated pool for the trial or are you comfortable with a reserved burst? For strict isolation and reproducibility of latency/throughput results we recommend a short dedicated pool for the 2-week window.

Proposed start date: 2027-03-08. If we lock eval set by 2027-03-04, we can stand up the environment and run initial baseline tests the following week.

I'll also coordinate with Marissa on any contract/ordering paperwork if we need short-term reserved capacity.

Thanks,
Lauren Bishop
